name: Keren-happuch
overview: Keren-happuch is a female figure in Scripture known primarily as a daughter of Job, as explicitly stated in Job 42:14. Beyond this unique attribute, there is no additional information about her tribe or other personal details. Her mention occurs in the context of Job's restored family after his trials.
namesAndTitles: The name Keren-happuch means 'horn of [cosmetic] eye shadow; i.e., cosmetic case,' revealing a cultural reference to beauty or adornment. This proper name is not indicated to have been given by God and is recorded in Job 42:14.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records Keren-happuch as a daughter of Job, emphasizing her place within Job's family after his period of suffering. No other family relationships beyond this are documented in the biblical text.
scriptureSignificance: Keren-happuch's significance lies in her role as part of the family God blessed Job with following his trials, symbolizing restoration and divine favor. Her mention underscores the completeness of Job's renewed blessings, including the birth of new children. Though not detailed extensively, her presence in the narrative highlights God's faithfulness to those who endure hardship.
